label: words
system:
You write the narration of a short vertical cutaway explainer video whose pictures are ALREADY planned and built: a 3D diorama where a thing is built step by step while one narrator talks. You get its beats in order. For each: its role in the story, what the viewer SEES on screen during it, the idea it carries, and its cue words (the animation fires on them). Write exactly one sentence per beat, in that order.
THE ONE RULE: each sentence says what is on screen in its beat, and nothing its beat does not show. Where the idea and the picture disagree, follow the picture.
Cue words: every cue word of a beat appears in its sentence exactly as written (the same spelling and form: not a plural, not another tense), where it reads naturally.
The account's formula (keep it):
HOOK      "If you [one naive physical action], you have a [thing]." (16 words or fewer)
CHAIN     "But [the visible consequence]." then "So you [add the part]." Every "But…" after the first names the part the fix before it added, or starts with "But now" (checked by code).
NAME      "This is a [real term]."
MYTH-BUST "And [the thing everyone knows] is not [what they think]." then what it really is.
FINISH    "Add [the finishing touches shown]." (they complete the thing itself: "Add rocks round the edge, lily pads and fish.") then "Congratulations, you have built a [thing]."
Facts: a number or a surprising claim only from the verified facts given, with their exact numbers. No other numbers.
Spoken forms (the narration is read aloud, then checked word by word): "cannot", never "can not"; no abbreviations: never "US", "U.S." or "USA" (write "American" or "America"), units in full ("square feet", "pounds", "gallons"); numbers as digits with a comma for thousands ("1,500"), years as 4 digits ("1952"), times as "3 AM" (never "a.m.").
Every fix solves the problem before it, and says how: it names the problem's own thing ("But dirt keeps falling in, so you add a filter that catches the dirt", never "so you add a pump").
A checked fact is said as it was checked: a range stays a range ("every 8 to 10 hours", never "once every 8 hours").
Say what is true about the thing, never what the picture or a prop does: no "a glowing outline traces it", no "as the page says".
Plain words, present tense, American English, sentences of 6-20 words, no questions, no lists of more than three, no "you might think". Each sentence ends with a full stop.
user:
Topic: submarine
Length: 30 s: 95-120 words in all, one sentence per beat (12 sentences).
Word budget: aim for 108 words in all, about 9 words a sentence (the hook up to 16; the name line and congrats short, so the others may run a little longer). Count before you answer: over 120 words is too long.
Verified facts (the only numbers and claims you may use, word for word where you use them):
- A submarine dives by letting sea water into its ballast tanks and surfaces by blowing it out with compressed air
- Navy attack submarines dive deeper than 800 feet; the exact depth is secret
- Water pressure rises by about one atmosphere for every 10 meters, or 33 feet, of depth

The beats, in order:
1. hook
   on screen: a sealed steel tube sits in the sea water. actions: dig dig; sea flood; sub show (on "tube")
   idea: seal a steel tube and put it in the sea and you have a submarine
   cue words: "tube"
2. problem
   on screen: the tube bobs up and down on the surface. actions: sub bob (on "floats")
   idea: it just floats and bobs on the surface
   cue words: "floats"
3. fix1
   on screen: glass tanks under the hull fill with water and the submarine sinks. actions: sub bobBack (on "So"); sub tanks (on "tanks"); sub flood (on "flood"); sub dive (on "sinks")
   idea: add ballast tanks that flood with sea water so it sinks
   cue words: "So", "tanks", "flood", "sinks"
4. problem2
   on screen: the submarine keeps sinking until it rests on the bottom. actions: sub diveBack; sub plunge
   idea: now it keeps sinking to the bottom and cannot come back up
   cue words: (none)
5. fix2
   on screen: yellow air tanks blow white air into the ballast tanks, the water empties and the submarine rises. actions: sub air (on "air"); sub blow (on "blow"); sub floodBack (on "blow"); sub plungeBack (on "blow")
   idea: compressed air blows the water out of the tanks and it rises
   cue words: "air", "blow"
   its fact: A submarine dives by letting sea water into its ballast tanks and surfaces by blowing it out with compressed air
6. name
   on screen: a glowing outline traces the ballast tanks. actions: ballast outline show (on "ballast")
   idea: this is a ballast tank
   cue words: "ballast"
7. how
   on screen: the tanks flood and the submarine dives. actions: ballast outline hide; sub flood (on "flood"); sub dive (on "dive")
   idea: flood the tanks to dive, blow them with air to rise
   cue words: "flood", "dive"
8. problem3
   on screen: yellow arrows press on the hull and dark cracks appear on it. actions: sub diveBack; sub plunge; squeeze show (on "pressure"); sub cracks (on "cracks")
   idea: deep down the water pressure cracks the hull
   cue words: "pressure", "cracks"
   its fact: Water pressure rises by about one atmosphere for every 10 meters, or 33 feet, of depth
9. fix3
   on screen: a thick steel hull wraps over the cracked one. actions: sub thick (on "hull"); sub cracksBack (on "hull"); squeeze hide (on "steel")
   idea: a thick round hull of strong steel holds the pressure
   cue words: "hull", "steel"
10. fact
   on screen: a depth counter behind the sea climbs to 800. actions: stand d show; depth show; depth count (on "800")
   idea: navy submarines dive deeper than 800 feet
   cue words: "800"
   its fact: Navy attack submarines dive deeper than 800 feet; the exact depth is secret
11. finish
   on screen: the submarine rises to the surface, a periscope slides up and the propeller spins. actions: depth hide (on "Add"); sub floodBack (on "Add"); sub plungeBack (on "Add"); sub periscope (on "periscope"); sub raise (on "propeller"); sub propeller (on "propeller"); sub spin (on "propeller")
   idea: add a periscope and a propeller
   cue words: "Add", "periscope", "propeller"
12. congrats
   on screen: the finished build, calm
   idea: you have built a submarine
   cue words: (none)
